verdicts.note: Married female engineering student; clearly female throughout.
Repeatedly self-identifies as doing civil engineering.
'my mum originally suggested it' maps to mother encouraged (agree).
Uncle studied civil but went into finance (not in industry) and she says she 'knew virtually nothing about it'; 'agree' overstates.
Chose A-levels by 'subjects I found interesting and that I was good at' = good at maths/science.
'knew virtually nothing about it' strongly supports choosing with little knowledge.
'more diverse' / 'wanted something quite diverse' clearly supports varied appeal.
'find it more interesting in the long run' supports interesting-work draw.
Quote is about avoiding a narrow qualification for career breadth, not explicitly science+maths without specialising; thin, downgrade.
Values the MEng's standing even though she may exit the profession.
Calls industry 'poorly paid'; salary not a draw, supports strongly disagree (low conf retained).
Did extensive careers research but 'engineering never came up' = no careers-advisor encouragement.
Mum suggested/encouraged it, so 'nobody encouraged me' is false = disagree.
No discouragement reported anywhere; quote answers the encourage/discourage probe with 'no'.
Answered 'I think so' then elaborated on wanting diversity; supports agree.
'The teaching has been excellent' = very satisfied.
Very positive about personal tutor ('great', keeps up to date).
Friends 'very motivating'; supports satisfaction with friends made.
Learnt leadership/managerial/group skills = course develops interpersonal skills.
Quote expresses what she WANTED (diversity), not satisfaction with delivered variety; thin, downgrade.
Questions relevance of modules ('never going to touch hydraulics again') = relevance hard to see.
Names 'sheer volume of work' as worst thing = dissatisfied with quantity of coursework.
'better off going straight through' = decided not to go on placement.
'haven't been able to find a job in the area' due to commuting constraint = no suitable-location placement.
Wants to get into industry a year earlier, but the 'finish ASAP to earn money' rationale is absent; primary driver is location. Thin, downgrade.
Saving the placement year ('one year earlier') reasonably maps to 4=time (low conf retained).
'I would need to work for a consultancy' over a contractor = consultancy preference.
'too ambitious' / needs 'future prospects... climb a ladder' = promotion very important.
'I certainly need to stay in one place' (husband's PhD) = location very important.
Flexible working listed as one acceptable option ('set or flexible'), emphasis on not over-long hours; thin, downgrade.
Quote is her personal stance against nurseries, not the importance of employer child-care policies when choosing a job; does not support the construct.
